title: Accept the Xcode license from Terminal
summary: After Xcode is installed, git or clang may stop with a message that you have not agreed to the Xcode license. You accept the license once in Terminal, which needs your administrator password.

error_patterns: You have not agreed to the Xcode license agreements
prerequisites: Full Xcode is installed from the App Store
You know your Mac administrator password

steps.explain: Check which developer tools are active. If it prints /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer, full Xcode is in use and you can continue. If it prints /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools, install Xcode from the App Store first.
Open the Xcode license in Terminal. Read it (press Space to scroll), then type agree at the end and press Return. Type your administrator password when asked; nothing is shown while you type.
steps.expect: The license text appears. After you type agree, the prompt returns without an error.

verify.expect: Two lines: Xcode version and Build version. No 'You have not agreed' message.

rollback.explain: There is no command that takes back a license you accepted. If you have not read the terms, do not type agree; press Ctrl+C to stop.

warnings: Accepting the license is a legal agreement for you or your organization. Read the terms before you type agree.
The command needs administrator rights (sudo). Type your password only in Terminal on your own Mac.
